name: PL-8177

lead: PL-8177 is an experimental oral peptide that activates the melanocortin 1 receptor, the receptor family linked to skin pigmentation. Tanning-peptide readers connect it to melanin signalling and a deeper tan.

It mimics alpha-MSH at MC1r. Its studied purpose is inflammation: preclinical work with PL-8177 and PL-8331 looked at preventing and reversing intestinal and ocular inflammation in animal models, and a phase 2a trial in active ulcerative colitis (n=16) began in September 2022. No studies were found of it for skin pigmentation or appearance.

paras: It has been used as an oral peptide in clinical research for ulcerative colitis. No tanning routine or timeline exists.
Not approved. Human safety data are limited to early-phase trials.

angle.text: PL-8177 is an MC1r agonist that tanning-peptide readers connect to melanocortin-driven melanin signalling and a deeper tan. It has been studied in inflammatory bowel and eye models.

lead: PL-8177 is an investigational oral peptide agonist of the melanocortin 1 receptor (MC1r). [1][2] It has been studied for inflammatory conditions, not for tanning or pigmentation: preclinical work with PL-8177 and PL-8331 examined prevention and reversal of intestinal and ocular inflammation in animal models. [1]
A phase 2a trial in active ulcerative colitis (n=16) began in September 2022. [2] No studies were found of PL-8177 for skin pigmentation or appearance.
